newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU Commission looking again at US GATT rice quotas.
newsitem.headline: EU Commission looking again at US GATT rice quotas.

text.p: The European Commission is revising a controversial regulation covering U.S. rice quotas to be allowed into the European Union under a GATT minimum access agreement, an EU official said on Tuesday.
"The Commission withdrew the proposal at last week's meeting of the cereals and rice management committee because it was clear that it would get a negative vote," the official said.
It is now revising the proposal which is unlikely to be put to the EU's cereals management committee again on Thursday, the official added.
"The Commission has not said what it is proposing to do with the regulation and it is unlikely to come up for discussion for at least two weeks," the official said.
The agreement has been fiercely opposed by the European rice trade for allowing the U.S. government to place management of their quota arrangements in the hands of trade organisations.
"The whole thing has been a mistake from the beginning. The U.S. government saw our negotiators coming and the result is a blank cheque for fraudsters," a trade source told Reuters.
The European Rice Association, the EU umbrella organisation for rice traders, has been campaigning against the arrangements on the grounds that they would lead to cross-subsidisation problems.

"The way the U.S. is proposing to allocate quotas would lead to problems of subsidisation. The European Rice Association has been campaigning for an end to the proposal and compensation under article 28 of the GATT agreement," a member told Reuters.
